research_concepts: absorption of the absent player's primary play types
minutes / initiations / same-position minutes as predictors
methodological_questions: Does the teammate closest in pre-absence initiation profile gain the most in the absent player's primary types more often than chance and more often than the minutes, initiation-volume and same-position heuristics?
How should a spell, a case, a primary type and a gain be defined so that gain is not a mechanical function of minutes or baseline volume?
Is n=148 spells from 11 cases enough once spells are clustered within cases?
How can regression to the mean, label error in derived play types and look-ahead in profile construction be controlled?

historical_evidence.finding: Connector absence displaced team offensive identity (D_A) more than usage-matched non-organizer absence (paired dD_A +0.1151, n=96 matched pairs; vs terminal +0.0777, n=25). Auto-tagged RISK:MECHANICAL_FLOOR and RISK:SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, LIM:small_sample.

A league-wide teammate DRIVE->PNR premium (+0.022 PPP, p=0.004) vanished to -0.006 (p=0.76) when PNR was restricted to inferrer-only labels; calibrated-label temporal contamination. Failure type C_artifact, RISK:LABEL_ERROR.

Case-study claim (+3.3 ORtg) had no CI or test, and its ranking target shared outcome data. 3 of 6 cases were labelled honest counter-examples. Failure mechanism E_unclear, RISK:LABEL_ERROR and RISK:BASE_RATE.
Star suppression cells were reported without placebo or matching; later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts (RISK:PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE).

Opponent 3-point luck has split-half reliability of about 0.004, while other player-level measures reached about 0.43-0.59 (MEASURE_RELIABILITY). Only indirectly relevant: it shows noisy per-player measures can carry no signal.
Player and teammate sequential premiums were reported on small cells (n≈30-70), with mechanism unclear. Limitations are label/classification error and small sample.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Teammate-sequence effect measured with calibrated (model-assisted) play-type labels
failed_approaches.why: The effect was an artifact of label construction and temporal contamination; it disappeared with inferrer-only labels.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Naming specific star/lineup effects without placebo or matching
failed_approaches.why: No placebo or matching; similar gaps were later treated as artifacts.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Case-study alignment claim with a ranking target that shares outcome data and no CI
failed_approaches.why: No CI or test reported; target shares outcome data; mechanism unclear.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Not a failure, but its limits apply here: absence-displacement analysis with a small matched sample
failed_approaches.why: Recorded limits are small sample and mechanical floor; the licensed comparison excludes organizers.

evidence_establishes: No retrieved record tested the exact question of whether the most similar, highest-minute, highest-initiation or same-position teammate is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.
Earlier absence work (FAM:SF-APPS-088) found large, significant displacement of team offensive identity when a connector is absent, using usage-matched controls. It does not say who absorbs the load.
Earlier records show that labelled-play-type effects can be artifacts of label construction (FAM:SF-CHT-032), and that unmatched or placebo-free comparisons have not been trusted (FAM:SF-CHT-009).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether teammate similarity predicts who absorbs the absent player's primary types.
The chance rate or the typical size of the largest gainer's share of redistributed possessions.
How reliable per-teammate play-type gain is within a spell.
Whether the 148 spells and 11 cases are independent or cover enough distinct absent players.
own_inferences: The four predictors (profile similarity, minutes, initiations, same-position minutes) are probably strongly correlated, so a hit for one will largely be a hit for the others. A fair test must be a head-to-head comparison against a chance baseline, not four separate confirmations.

Absorption is partly mechanical. The player who gains the most minutes after the absence, usually the replacement or a starter, will gain the most possessions. Gain should be normalized per minute, or minutes change should be modeled.
With about 7-9 rotation teammates, chance for 'largest gainer' is about 11-15%, so even a real heuristic will probably have a modest hit rate. Detecting it needs many independent absent-player cases.
With 11 cases, spells within a case share roster, coach and opponent context. Effective sample size is closer to 11 than 148 for the question of whether a heuristic generalizes.

Per-spell gain for a single teammate is noisy (small possession counts). The identity of the 'largest gainer' therefore has low reliability and regression to the mean is likely: the teammate with the largest observed gain will tend to have been lucky.
uncertainties: The meaning of 'spell' and 'case' in the stated n=148 / 11 is not given, and neither is the definition of 'primary types'.
Whether play-type labels in the possession graph are inferrer-only or calibrated (FAM:SF-CHT-032 shows this matters).
The cause of absence (injury, rest, ejection, trade) and its timing are unknown, as is whether the minutes change is exogenous.
The distribution of spell lengths and the number of possessions in the absent player's primary types per spell are unknown.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieved records did not answer the question, but they changed the design and moved the decision from a plain proceed to proceed_with_changes. Records on label artifacts (FAM:SF-CHT-032), missing placebo or matching (FAM:SF-CHT-009) and small-sample / mechanical-floor limits (FAM:SF-APPS-088) require inferrer-only labels, a chance/placebo baseline, per-minute normalization and cluster-level inference.

blocking_constraints.text: 11 cases means about 11 independent clusters. A hit rate modestly above the roughly 12-15% chance rate cannot be established at cluster level; 148 spells overstate the information.
The largest gainer in raw possessions is mechanically the teammate who gains the most minutes or has the highest baseline usage, so heuristic hits can be tautological unless normalized.

prior_work.summary: Retrieved work covers adjacent topics (team identity displacement after connector absence, label-artifact risk, unplaceboed lineup effects). None tested heuristic prediction of the largest teammate gainer in the absent player's primary types.

risks.text: Only 11 cases; spells are clustered within cases, so the effective n is small and power for hit-rate differences is low.

Gains in counts scale with minutes and baseline volume; low-baseline players have a floor, high-baseline players a larger room to gain. Without per-minute normalization the minutes heuristic wins trivially.
Selecting the 'largest gainer' picks the extreme of noisy per-teammate changes; spells are probably selected for notable absences.
Per-teammate play-type counts in short absences are small and noisy; reliability of the gainer identity is untested (cf. the near-zero reliability found for opponent 3-point luck in FAM:SF-PAP-068).
Derived play-type labels can be artifacts (FAM:SF-CHT-032). Primary types should use inferrer-only labels or be checked for label sensitivity.
The pre-absence profile must use only games before the absence; using full-season data would leak absence-period behavior into the similarity measure.
Opponent, lineup, injury status of other teammates, garbage time, coach changes, and the replacement's entry all affect who absorbs possessions. Similarity correlates with position and minutes.
Chance of picking the largest gainer depends on the number of eligible teammates; the null must be computed per spell.
Four heuristics and multiple definitions of similarity and primary types give many comparisons; one primary comparison must be fixed.
Four seasons of rule, style and tracking changes; roster and role evolution within a season may confound pre/post comparisons.

design.estimand: For each absence spell, the largest gainer is the teammate with the largest increase in per-100-team-possessions initiations in the absent player's primary types (the top play types accounting for at least 60% of the absent player's pre-absence initiations; at most three types), measured versus that teammate's own pre-absence baseline. The estimand is the hit rate of each heuristic (closest pre-absence initiation-profile distance; most minutes; most total initiations; most same-position minutes) at naming the largest gainer, relative to the per-spell chance rate (1/number of eligible teammates) and relative to the other heuristics. Primary comparison: profile similarity versus the best of the other three heuristics, using hit rate above chance.
design.unit: Absence spell (team, absent player, contiguous set of missed games) nested within case (absent player-season). Inference is clustered at case level.
design.sample: All spells meeting pre-registered criteria: absent player with at least 20 pre-absence games and at least 100 initiations in their primary types; at least 3 games missed; at least 8 teammates in the rotation; exclude ejections and in-game injuries, trades and mid-spell major roster changes. Teammates must have at least 10 games and 15 minutes per game of overlap before the spell. Use regular season and playoffs, 2022-23 to 2025-26. Expected about 148 spells from 11 cases per the task statement; report the exact flow and the number of distinct absent players before analysis.
design.power: Chance per spell is about 1/7 to 1/9 (about 11-14%). Treating 148 spells as independent, SE of the hit rate is about 0.03 and a true hit rate of about 25% would be detectable at about 80% power. Clustering in 11 cases roughly reduces effective n to the case level; at the cluster level, only large effects (hit rate roughly above 40%) would be detectable. Pre-register the case-level cluster bootstrap and report an MDE with it; if the realized effective n gives MDE above 40% hit rate, report the result as underpowered and not as a null.
design.controls: Normalize gain per 100 team possessions and per minute (and report a minutes-adjusted version: gain residual after regressing on change in minutes). Compute similarity from pre-absence games only (profile = share of initiations by play type, cosine or Jensen-Shannon distance; fixed before looking at outcomes). Use inferrer-only play-type labels with a calibrated-label sensitivity check. Shrink noisy per-teammate gains with empirical-Bayes using a split-half reliability estimate, and report that reliability. Include a placebo: assign each spell a random game window of equal length with the absent player present and test the same heuristics. Compare to a random-teammate null and to a permutation null within spell.
design.falsification: The hypothesis is rejected if the case-clustered 95% CI for profile-similarity hit rate minus chance excludes values above 10 percentage points, or if similarity does not beat the minutes heuristic after normalization. If the placebo windows show hit rates comparable to those during absences, the effect is attributed to a mechanical or baseline-volume artifact. If the result disappears when minutes change is controlled, label as mechanical.
design.multiplicity: One primary comparison (profile similarity vs best other heuristic, hit rate). The other three heuristics and any secondary similarity metrics are reported as secondary with Holm correction. No post-hoc redefinition of primary types or similarity.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if profile-similarity hit rate exceeds chance by at least 10 percentage points with a case-clustered 95% CI excluding zero, beats the best other heuristic, and survives the minutes-adjusted and placebo checks. Rejected only if adequately powered (MDE ≤ 15 points). Otherwise report as inconclusive/underpowered.
design.data_version: Freeze NBA stats API play-by-play, rotation, starter and box-score files and the possession graph for 2022-23 to 2025-26 (regular season and playoffs, all complete as of 2026-11-01); record file hashes and the label version before analysis. Pre-register code and thresholds before looking at gains.

You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 4 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
